Vision, Values and Ethos
Vision, Values and Ethos
In the Learning in Harmony Trust, we work in harmony to achieve excellence for all.
We believe that doing things in harmony means a commitment to working collaboratively and effectively using everyone’s strengths to meet a common aim. We do not follow a school-in-a-box model and instead work collaboratively at all levels within and across each school to maximise potential through continuous challenge and support.
We live and breathe our values and focus on doing things the right way, providing the perfect environment for all our children to flourish and succeed. And with a diverse range of schools in two contrasting locations, we offer a unique opportunity for professionals looking for a challenging and rewarding career in a supportive, creative and forward-thinking environment.
A nurturing community
Acting with integrity
Encouraging innovation

Welcome
Welcome
Thank you for taking the time to find out more about Joseph Clarke School – a centre of excellence for pupils aged 3 to 19 with vision impairment and/or additional needs. Situated in Waltham Forest, we are a small, inclusive and nurturing school welcoming pupils from across London and surrounding counties.
As a part of Learning in Harmony Trust, our mission is to enable our pupils to flourish, lead independent and fulfilling lives and make a positive impact on the world. We do this through our Education Charter which sets out how we meet the educational and pastoral needs of our pupils and ensure every day is a positive, safe and meaningful one.
Providing enjoyable, high-quality holistic learning opportunities is at the very heart of our approach and, as experts in supporting pupils with vision impairment, we give them the knowledge, tools and confidence to develop their love of learning. In doing so, we harness the very best technology to assist them in their learning and lives.
As a close-knit school, we take the time to properly get to know our pupils. As such, we are able to develop personalised learning pathways so that every pupil makes the progress that is right for them and gains the qualifications they need to progress successfully onto the next stage of their education and lives.
I am very proud of the community we have created at Joseph Clarke School. With the hard work and commitment of our fantastic staff and the excellent partnerships we have with our parents and carers, our pupils thrive here – both educationally and socially. But, most importantly, our pupils feel happy and safe here and greet me each morning with a smile on their faces ready for the day ahead.
To find out more about us, please come and visit us and see what our pupils are achieving here. Alternatively, if you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me at the school.
I look forward to meeting you.
Chadia Filali-MouteiPrincipal

Careers Programme
Careers at Joseph Clarke School
Preparing learners for the future. No aspiration is too high.
Our vision
Careers education is not a one-off event or an extra lesson. It is part of how we prepare learners for adulthood. We support learners’ aspirations and help them make informed decisions about their next steps towards their career ambitions.
Meet the Team
Sam McCarthy -Careers Leader/Advisor (sam.mccarthy@lihtrust.uk)
Ross Burrell - SLT Careers Leader (ross.burrell@lihtrust.uk)
Suggestion box: please support us with making any suggestions this could be as simple as a contact for a careers fair
Providers are welcome to leave a copy of their prospectus or other relevant course literature with Ross Burrell or Sam McCarthy, Career Leader. This will be made available to pupils and families as appropriate.
What does Careers look like at Joseph Clarke School?
Schools are required to ensure that there is an opportunity for a range of education and training providers to access students in years 7 to 13 for the purposes of informing them about approved technical education, qualifications or apprenticeships.
Schools must also have a policy statement that outlines the circumstances in which education and training providers will be given access to these students.
This is outlined in section 42B of the Education Act 1997, the Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022 and on page 43 of guidance from the Department for Education (DfE) on careers guidance and access for education and training providers.
We have dedicated careers lessons, a Calendar of Careers activities including Careers fairs, Workshops, Trips and Visits. Curriculum content and lessons make links to Careers wherever possible. We also support learners through dedicated careers lessons. Learners can access one-to-one Careers Interviews by a trained professional tailored to meet the needs of our learners. Through high-quality Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG), we inspire every learner to recognise their potential, raise their aspirations and confidently shape their future. We are committed to equipping our young people with the knowledge, skills, experiences and resilience they need to make informed choices, embrace opportunities and thrive in life beyond school.
A future shaped around our learners
Success looks different for every learner. Whether their next step involves further education, a supported internship or greater independence in the community, we work with each young person and their family to plan a meaningful path forward.
Gatsby benchmarks are used as a Framework for Careers, and we record careers-related activities using Compass+.
Impact of the Career Programme at Joseph Clarke
The career programme at Joseph Clarke helps pupils build practical skills, explore their interests and prepare for life after school. It offers experiences and guidance tailored to each pupil’s strengths, needs and aspirations.
Skills and work readiness. Pupils develop communication, teamwork and time management skills through activities such as school-based work experience. These opportunities help them understand workplace routines and different job roles.
Individual career pathways. Staff use EHC plans, observations and conversations with pupils to identify their interests and aspirations. Parents and carers also contribute, helping to shape a career profile and plan that reflects each pupil.
Career awareness. Storytelling, role-play and discussion introduce pupils to different careers. Guest speakers, career videos, virtual visits and employer workshops give them further opportunities to explore the world of work.
Experience and employment options. Career fairs, workplace visits and partnerships with local employers help pupils meet professionals and try practical activities. Pupils also learn about apprenticeships, supported employment and other pathways suited to their needs.
Transitions after school. Personalised guidance helps pupils consider college, vocational training, supported internships and other post-16 options. College visits and meetings with careers advisers support pupils and families in planning their next steps.
How the school measures and assesses the impact of the careers programme on pupils
Evaluations of the careers programme are taken at various times, to include the following:
After learners complete a careers work experience.
Learners have one-page career profiles.
Weekly updating of a Careers Tracker
Some learners will complete BTEC Work skills.
Mock interviews are completed through workshops.
Key Documents
Provider Access Document
Work Experience
We offer different work-related opportunities both internally and externally - including within our Louis Training Cafe, which is open to the public, our primary classes at school, the Reprographics department and with our Site Services Team. External work-related opportunities include local shops such as The Community Store and Tesco. We also have a partnership with a local horticulture co-operative, Organiclea.
We support learners to access work-related experiences that focus on their interests where possible. Last term, one of our learners with an interest in politics and diplomacy worked in the office of a local Member of Parliament - Sir Iain Duncan Smith. The learner reflected on this as being an amazing experience.
Working with Organisations
We work with a range of organisations who offer mentoring to our learners, including Blind in Business, OrganicLea, Aston Group Employer workshops, DWP Financial literacy/Employability Workshops, and the Heaven House Enterprise project. We have also had a successful visit to Leyton Orient Football Club and attended a Pizza Express Workshop.
Upcoming Activities - Learners and Parents/Carers

This information has been reviewed in September 2026. The next scheduled review for this information is in July 2027.

pageCache.pageTitle: Joseph Clarke School - Literacy and Reading
pageCache.text:
Part of the Learning in Harmony Trust
"In the Learning in Harmony Trust, we work in harmony to achieve excellence for all. We live and breathe our values and focus on doing things the right way, providing the perfect environment for all our children to flourish and succeed. And with a diverse range of schools in two contrasting locations, we offer a unique opportunity for professionals looking for a challenging and rewarding career in a supportive, creative and forward-thinking environment." Click here to find out more about the LiH Trust.
Literacy and Reading
Literacy and Reading
Literacy and Reading
We believe that good literacy skills are the key to unlocking the curriculum. Whether pupils learn to read using Braille or print, we are determined to give them the literacy skills they need to access the curriculum in full, become independent learners where possible, and nurture a love of reading and stories.
By beginning with phonics at an early age, we aim to lay firm foundations for literacy and seek to build on them throughout a pupil’s time with us. Like all learning at Joseph Clarke School, we always respond to each pupil’s individual needs which means pupils learn at their own pace using methods that best suit their needs. For some pupils, this will mean using an Intensive Interaction approach to communication and tactile signs and symbols. Some pupils will follow a Functional Approach to Braille focussing on key vocabulary whilst others go on to use Braille as their primary medium.
Phonics at Joseph Clarke School
At Joseph Clarke School we feel that learning to read using either braille or print is an essential part of developing independent learners and a life skill that will be used beyond a pupil’s schooling with us. Teaching of phonics and the development of reading for each pupil personalised according to each pupil’s individual needs. This may involve communication development, sound awareness, playing with sounds, reading their name, functional reading skills that will impact upon a student’s independence skills, or reading to access the curriculum which could then lead to a love of reading for pleasure throughout their lives.
Why phonics is used to develop reading and spelling?
Phonological awareness is an important aspect of the development of phonics for reading and spelling. It also plays an important role in the development of vocabulary and impacts on the development of grammar and comprehension skills.
During the early stages of reading, phonics is taught as a way of decoding written letters and spoken sounds. As their knowledge and use of phonics is practised and consolidated, pupils will need to focus less on the actual decoding of words which then allows them to focus on the understanding and meaning within a text.
The teaching and learning of phonics
At Joseph Clarke school we are committed to ensuring our pupils develop their phonic skills to enable them the best possible chance in becoming lifelong readers. We use the Read Write Inc (RWI) programme which follows a method of teaching reading and writing, centred on learning the sounds of the letters and then blending them together to read words. The children will also learn to break down words into individual sounds in order to support them along their journey of developing their writing skills.
The stage in which the children at Joseph Clarke begin will be determined by the pathway they are on but children will initially learn the single letter sounds and begin to blend these together. Once the children have been taught all of the single letter sounds they will be assessed and grouped according to their ability and or provided the necessary support within the classroom delivered by either the teacher or support staff. The children will be taught in small groups delivered by either teachers or support staff who have had the appropriate Read Write Inc training, which means learning can be tailored to meet the individual needs of each child and in line with their Education Health Care Plans.
Read Write Inc will commence in Reception and children will continue their RWI learning throughout their primary and secondary experience (depending on pathway and ability) and will have at least four sessions per week, lasting 20-30 minutes. Children will be assessed every half term to track their progress and to ensure they are working within the appropriate group. All children will begin by learning the Set 1 sounds in a specific order and progress through each set at their own speed and according to ability.
Children will also begin learning to blend sounds together to make words after learning the first 5 sounds, firstly through practising oral blending.
Once children can blend independently, they will progress on to reading green words. After they can read green words, children will move on to begin reading stories in their sessions. Each storybook is matched to the sounds the children have grown familiar to, which supports the transition onto the next stage and aids them to build their confidence with reading. The children are exposed to and start to learn the red words through these storybooks, which are irregular words that cannot be sounded out using Fred talk. The process is repetitive and supports learning at Joseph Clarke, as it builds upon a consistent a systematic approach as each storybook is taught in the same way, with children practising reading the green words in the story and also the red words, before they begin to read the book. Children will then read the book several times to help build their fluency and comprehension skills.
Phonics Implementation and Impact at Joseph Clarke School
Read Write Inc tutors will plan (according to need and ability) for the children to work with a partner as Talking is an important part of the process as it provides opportunities for children to support each other with orally building their sentences and writing their ideas down.
Praise plays a significant part in encouraging children to engage with their phonics learning at Joseph Clarke School and this will be carried out in accordance to the environment and context of children.
Assessment is ongoing in response to our pupils needs but formal assessment will take place termly for those pupils identified.
Phonic Sets. The sounds are broken into three sets and children will only move onto the next set when they are confident blending and recognising the previous set.
Students who use braille:
When teaching phonics, we include adaptations for braille users; the order of learning sounds in Read Write Inc and learning of the braille letters is different. This means the early stages of phonics for braille readers may involve more oral learning alongside presentation of the braille grapheme prior to learning of the specific recorded braille letters. This stage is carefully assessed and tracked using our assessment materials to show progress and highlight areas to develop further.
Students with complex needs:
Communication development is essential for students with complex needs and the daily routines and short phrases that are repeated and linked to the daily routines, are essential. Playing with sounds and words is an enjoyable way of introducing sounds awareness to students with complex needs. The focus can then be on words that are important to the pupil and these words are incorporated into personalised stories as appropriate to their needs
How will Joseph Clarke parents be supported and encouraged to support at home?
It’s very important even if a child is not at the stage of reading words, to have stories read to them. Parents/carers will be invited to parent meetings, provided with information to support learning in school and sent links to short clips to watch, which will explain the benefits of reading to their child, including encouraging parents/carers to:
Reading for Pleasure at Joseph Clarke School:
We recognise that reading for pleasure directly links to our pupils’ success beyond the classroom, throughout their time at school, to support their quality of life now, and into adulthood.
We firmly believe reading for pleasure also supports our pupils’ well-being, empathy, their ability to gain insights into the world, others viewpoints and supports their independent living skills.
At JCS, we promote our pupils’ reading for pleasure in a number of ways:
Listen to child read regularly.
Discuss the different features of various books.
Explain the meaning of new words.
Local library visits and Book Clubs.

Remote Learning
Remote Learning
If pupils spend time away from school during the term as a result of extended illness or because they have significant medical needs, they will receive a personalised remote learning offer.
Each pupil’s teacher will work with families to devise a remote learning curriculum that is right for them but it is likely to include a combination of online sessions, learning tasks presented through Google Classroom, and physical resources sent home.
Whilst pupils may not be physically in school, our teachers and support staff are always on-hand to support pupils and their families in whichever way they need.

Lockdown Procedures
Lockdown Procedures
The safety and wellbeing of our pupils and staff is our highest priority. As part of our safeguarding arrangements and in line with statutory requirements, the academy has clear procedures in place for a range of situations, including the use of a ‘lockdown’ where necessary. A lockdown may be implemented if there is a potential risk to the school or in the wider local area, and it is considered safer for everyone to remain inside the building while the situation is assessed. This procedure is precautionary and forms part of our wider approach to maintaining a safe and secure environment, in line with national guidance and statutory responsibilities.
From time to time, schools may practise these procedures with staff and pupils to ensure everyone is familiar with the process and knows how to respond calmly and effectively.
In the event of a real lockdown, the school will communicate with parents and carers as soon as it is safe to do so. During this time, we ask that parents and carers do not contact their child, phone the school or come to the site so that the situation can be managed safely and effectively.
We appreciate the continued support of our families in helping us keep our school communities safe.

Mobility and Independence
Mobility and Independence
We aim to support our pupils to gain the freedom and independence they may want in the future. We, therefore, do everything we can to equip them with the skills they need to keep themselves safely independent.
Mobility is about enabling a pupil to realise their potential regarding independent movement. This could be as simple as encouraging a pupil to explore the area around them through the use of all their senses and adapted mobility aids or as complex as carrying out a journey on public transport independently using long-cane skills.
Our mobility and independence program covers posture and spatial awareness, pre-cane and cane skills, sighted guide skills as well as environmental awareness. We also teach pupils about road safety, public transportation, personal safety as well as everyday skills such as eating and dressing.
Our habilitation team works alongside pupils as they develop these important skills and are always on hand to offer families practical advice and tips. They can be reached at:
Email: nicola.hobart@lihtrust.uk
Telephone: 020 8523 4833

Ofsted & School Performance
Joseph Clarke School – Performance Report
The students at Joseph Clarke School are a wide cohort of individuals with significantly different strengths and areas of need. When thinking about measures of the school’s performance we look at not only the achievement of students in accredited subjects but also at their progress in the development of their communication and social skills. For our students with significant vision impairment, we also review their achievements within the Curriculum Framework for Vision Impairment (CFVI) which may include their knowledge of the Braille code, their ability to find their way around the school building using their long cane or the development of their independence skills when using magnifying or screen reader software or other assistive technology such as refreshable braille displays and electronic Braille notetakers.

Operation Encompass
Operation Encompass
At our school, we are part of Operation Encompass. This is a joint partnership between police and education, designed to enable schools to offer immediate support to children experiencing domestic abuse.
If the police attend a domestic abuse incident where a child is present or involved, they will notify the school’s Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) before the start of the next school day.
This sharing of information enables appropriate support to be given, dependent upon the needs and wishes of the child, ensuring that no child has to face the aftermath of a difficult situation alone.

RSHE
RSHE
For primary-aged children, the key updates include:
For secondary-aged children, the key updates include:
Approach to Teaching
At Joseph Clarke School, our RSHE curriculum is designed to empower pupils with the knowledge, skills and values they need to lead safe, healthy, respectful and fulfilling lives. Rooted in care, inclusivity and age-appropriate progression, our curriculum promotes the personal, social and emotional development of every child.
Drawing on the Statutory Guidance for Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE), alongside specialist resources from Oak National Academy and the PSHE Association, our provision supports pupils in understanding themselves, building positive relationships and navigating an increasingly complex world.
Through carefully sequenced, pupil-centred learning, pupils explore themes such as friendship, emotions, physical and mental health, rights, identity and equality. They are encouraged to think critically, communicate effectively and act with empathy, confidence and responsibility. Our curriculum creates a respectful and supportive environment that prepares pupils for the opportunities and challenges of modern life, both now and in the future.
As a specialist school, we recognise that every pupil develops at their own pace and that learning in RSHE must be tailored to meet individual needs. We carefully adapt the content, language and delivery of lessons so that pupils can access learning in ways that are meaningful and appropriate for them. This may include simplifying or pre-teaching vocabulary, using line drawings, tactile resources or objects of reference, providing audio description, adapting communication methods, or presenting information through a range of accessible formats. Our teachers use their knowledge of each pupil to judge when they are ready to explore new concepts, revisiting learning where needed and ensuring that sensitive topics are introduced in a safe, supportive and developmentally appropriate way. This personalised approach enables every pupil to build understanding, confidence and independence at a pace that is right for them.
RSHE is taught primarily through dedicated PSHE lessons, where pupils develop their understanding in a structured and progressive way. These key concepts are then revisited, reinforced and contextualised across the wider curriculum. For example, pupils explore themes such as resilience, diversity and different family structures through literature in English, while online safety and responsible digital citizenship are developed through Digital Skills lessons. This cross-curricular approach helps pupils make meaningful connections between their learning and the wider world.
Our RSHE curriculum is always delivered by class teachers, who know their pupils well and are best placed to provide a safe, supportive and responsive learning environment. Our Community
Our Community
We have a strong sense of community at Joseph Clarke School and believe that by caring for and supporting each other we can fulfil our vision. We extend a very warm welcome to every new pupil joining our school and help them to settle into our school routines and environment as quickly as possible.
Pupils form lifelong friendships with peers as well as positive and trusting relationships with their teachers. As a result, pupils feel safe and secure and have the confidence to grasp every opportunity on offer and make the most of their time with us.
We are pleased to welcome children and young people from across London and the surrounding counties, from a range of different backgrounds. We are proud that our pupils represent so many diverse communities and we take every opportunity to learn about and celebrate each other’s cultures and religions.
Families are an integral part of our school community and we encourage them to be actively involved in their child’s education and in the life of the school.
